title: SnSe thermoelectric performance enhanced by vacancy engineering
abstract: Tin selenide (SnSe) exhibits high thermoelectric figure of merit ZT. Recent polycrystalline work argues Sn vacancy scattering dominates lattice thermal conductivity reduction. Challenges remain in reproducing high ZT across batches.
full_text: Tin selenide (SnSe) exhibits high thermoelectric figure of merit ZT along the b-axis in single crystals. Recent polycrystalline campaigns conclude that Sn vacancy scattering is the dominant mechanism that suppresses lattice thermal conductivity κ_L, outweighing intrinsic anharmonicity under device-relevant sintering. Comparative measurements show batch-to-batch variation in ZT when polycrystalline samples are sintered under different Sn-rich atmospheres. Challenges remain in reproducing high ZT across batches. Future work should quantify vacancy concentration versus κ_L with controlled defect metrology.

title: PbTe-based nanocomposites for power factor optimization
abstract: Lead telluride (PbTe) nanocomposites improve power factor via energy filtering. DFT calculations support resonant doping. Experimental validation is limited for some dopant chemistries and long-term stability is unclear.
full_text: Lead telluride (PbTe) nanocomposites improve power factor via energy filtering at nano-precipitate interfaces. DFT calculations support resonant doping near the valence band edge. Experimental sections report Seebeck and electrical conductivity for selected dopants, but experimental validation is limited for some dopant chemistries. Long-term stability under thermal cycling is unclear, and oxidation at grain boundaries may confound energy-filtering claims. Process windows for spark plasma sintering are only partially mapped.

title: Machine learning accelerated screening of half-Heusler thermoelectrics
abstract: A machine learning model screens half-Heusler compounds for thermoelectric properties. Band gap and thermal conductivity descriptors are used. However, synthesis constraints and phase stability are not fully integrated, leaving a method gap toward closed-loop discovery.
full_text: A machine learning model screens half-Heusler compounds for thermoelectric properties using band gap and thermal conductivity descriptors. Cross-validation metrics look strong on the training distribution. However, synthesis constraints and phase stability are not fully integrated into the ranking objective, leaving a method gap toward closed-loop discovery. Candidates that look promising on paper may sit above the convex hull or require unavailable precursors. Coupling the ML ranker to Materials Project / OQMD filters is recommended before experimental campaigns.

title: Early SnSe single crystals: ultralow κ_L attributed to lattice anharmonicity
abstract: Early tin selenide (SnSe) single-crystal studies attribute ultralow lattice thermal conductivity primarily to strong lattice anharmonicity rather than vacancy scattering. Vacancy contributions are treated as secondary.
full_text: Early tin selenide (SnSe) single-crystal studies attribute ultralow lattice thermal conductivity κ_L primarily to strong lattice anharmonicity and soft phonon modes rather than vacancy scattering. Vacancy contributions are treated as secondary under the reported growth conditions. The narrative emphasizes intrinsic bonding anharmonicity as sufficient to explain ultralow κ_L without invoking defect engineering. Later polycrystalline vacancy-focused claims should be compared under normalized measurement conditions.

title: Mg3Sb2 thermoelectrics: from DFT prediction to spark plasma synthesis
abstract: Mg3Sb2 emerges as a promising n-type thermoelectric. DFT predicts favorable band features. Spark plasma sintering synthesis conditions strongly affect ZT. Limitations include air sensitivity and dopant solubility windows that are not fully mapped.
full_text: Mg3Sb2 emerges as a promising n-type thermoelectric. DFT predicts favorable band features near the conduction band edge. Spark plasma sintering synthesis conditions strongly affect ZT through grain size and secondary-phase formation. Limitations include air sensitivity during powder handling and dopant solubility windows that are not fully mapped. Process–property coupling remains a bottleneck between computational screening and device-ready pellets.
